Houston Price Check

We trained a model on Houston listings to estimate what each home should cost from its size, age, type and location. Search by what you can pay each month, and see how each listing compares with similar homes nearby.

How the model got better

Same algorithm each time (gradient-boosted trees, trained on log price). Only the inputs change. Median % error on 4,489 test homes the model never trained on. Shorter is better.

"Below similar homes" means worth a closer look: ask the agent why it is cheaper. The data can't see condition or flood history. Click a row to see its monthly cost.

How it works

  1. Clean

    Zillow listings → homes. Dropped vacant land, duplicates and outliers; fixed lot sizes that mixed acres and square feet; treated median-filled values as unknown.

  2. Build features

    House facts, plus miles to Downtown, the Medical Center, the Galleria, the Energy Corridor and UH, plus neighborhood comps: the median $/sqft of the 10 nearest homes, built so a home never sees its own price.

  3. Train and test

    Gradient-boosted trees on log price, scored on homes held out from training. Zillow's Zestimate was kept out of training because it sits within about 3% of the list price.

  4. Price check and budget

    Every home gets a fair value from a model that never saw it. Only homes where the model is reliable are rated: single-family and townhouses built 1980 or later, under 1 acre, $150k–$1.2M.

What it can't do

  • List prices aren't sale prices, and this is one snapshot of listings from June 2024.
  • The model can't see condition, renovations or flood history. Our first version flagged "bargains" that turned out to be model mistakes (huge lots, very old homes, manufactured homes), so those are no longer rated.
  • New-build communities share map coordinates, which flatters the neighborhood comps.
  • Tax and insurance rates are Texas averages; HOA fees and flood insurance aren't included.
Data: Houston Housing Market 2024 (Zillow listings, June 2024) via Kaggle, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Built for the CodeCoogs UH AI Hackathon, Fall 2026.
